title: 12-name watchlist · 4 November 2026, 20:00 SGT
summary: Google plans a US$15 billion Malaysian infrastructure investment in 2027–2028, according to Reuters. Meta launched its first euro bond offering and filed preliminary terms, with pricing still unverified. A separate Reuters update records US futures recovering from early election-related losses. All twelve main prices remain saved 3 November regular closes; seven separately dated premarket observations are included. Watch only, not holdings or calls.
coverage_note: Fixed cutoff: 4 November 2026, 20:00 SGT (12:00 UTC). Review interval: 16:00–20:00 SGT, with overlap from 15:45 SGT (07:45 UTC), compared against the prior durable editions. Source checking occurred after cutoff; only developments and quotes timestamped at or before cutoff are included. Reuters and issuer-news coverage is partial, not a complete wire census. Prior research, qualifications and after-hours observations remain in unchanged archives. The existing schema contains the original twelve names; requested SPY, QQQ, TLT, IEI and IEF additions are not represented as verified quote coverage in this edition.
price_basis: Main prices are USD completed regular-session observations for 3 November 2026 at 16:00 EST (4 November 05:00 SGT), with original vendor timestamp precision retained. Daily change compares the 2 November ordinary close. These are saved prior closes, not live or exact 20:00 SGT prices. Separate premarket observations for NVDA, GOOGL, BRK.B, AMD, MU, TSLA and TSM are dated 4 November, 06:40–06:56 EST (19:40–19:56 SGT), with minute precision and changes against the 3 November close. They are saved observations, not live prices or return endpoints. Five later premarket observations were excluded. TSM is the US-listed USD ADR.
return_basis: Cumulative return = 100 × (3 November 2026 adjusted close ÷ baseline adjusted close − 1). The 1–6 calendar-month baselines are 2 October, 3 September, 3 August, 2 July, 3 June and 1 May 2026. October 3 and May 3 fall on weekends; July 3 is the observed US Independence Day market holiday, so preceding sessions are used. All 72 dated inputs were independently checked. Adjusted closes incorporate split and dividend/distribution adjustments; ordinary previous closes remain separate. These are cumulative returns before fees and taxes, not six individual monthly returns.
caveats: All twelve regular and previous closes and all 72 dated adjusted-close baselines were freshly reconfirmed. The regular-price and return numbers are unchanged. Daily changes, six cumulative horizons and seven included premarket changes were independently recomputed.

Direct Stock Analysis requests returned HTTP 403; accessible indexed tables and fresh pages were used. Indexed observations can lag vendor changes. A Broadcom historical-table result showed 332.75, but its fresh close header and Yahoo dated history agree on 332.13; the inconsistent result was excluded. Stale and differently adjusted alternatives were not substituted.

Premarket coverage is intentionally partial. Apple, Microsoft, Amazon, Meta and Broadcom observations were later than the fixed cutoff and were not backdated. Yahoo observations lacking an explicit calendar date were not substituted. Earlier after-hours snapshots remain in their original reports.

Meta’s primary SEC prospectus is preliminary and leaves euro offering size, coupons and maturities unfilled. Reuters reports an offering launch, not verified final pricing or settlement. The earlier $15 billion USD pricing is a separate transaction already covered.

Google’s Malaysian investment is attributed to Reuters reporting of the company announcement. A matching original $15 billion issuer release was not retrieved; the accessible regional issuer index still showed the earlier $160 million water-infrastructure announcement. Investment plans are not realised spending or booked revenue.

All twelve issuer SEC recent-submission feeds were checked. Only Meta’s 11:01:27 UTC filing fell in the review window. These feeds do not constitute a census of all third-party ownership filings or company news.

Apple’s RSS was empty; Alphabet, Meta and Micron news lists were incomplete in the accessible rendering. Other issuer homepages and targeted Reuters searches do not guarantee comprehensive coverage. No new verified company item is not proof of no news.

The shared Reuters market update is kept separate from issuer announcements. Its 05:02 EST publication describes earlier market observations and possible policy risks, not enacted restrictions or the cause of a specific stock’s price move.
The older AMD warrant-number discrepancy, Tesla consumer-group complaint, Nvidia China-exposure qualification and other prior items are preserved in earlier reports and are not relabelled as new.
Watch only: no user holding, executed trade, buy call or recommendation is implied. No private diary, account information, restricted screenshot or analyst-house report is reproduced.

rows.name: NVIDIA

research.headline: Shared watchlist context: Reuters reports futures reversing early election losses
facts: Reuters’ 05:02 EST (10:02 UTC) update reports US equity futures recovering from early losses after the midterm results. The article’s specific futures snapshot is earlier, at 04:22 EST.

The report describes mixed hyperscaler shares and gains in AMD and other chip stocks during early premarket trading. These report-time observations are not the separate saved quote snapshots in this edition.
research.analysis: The reversal shows why early election reactions should not be treated as a stable forecast. Possible AI-policy scrutiny remains a scenario, not an enacted restriction.
research.risks: Election interpretation, policy expectations and thin premarket trading can change rapidly. News association does not demonstrate causation for a particular share move.
research.next_watch: The regular US session and specific policy or issuer announcements rather than extrapolation from initial futures moves.

rows.name: Alphabet Class A

research.headline: Google plans US$15 billion Malaysian infrastructure investment for 2027–2028
facts: Reuters reported at 09:13:54 UTC that Google plans US$15 billion of Malaysian investment over 2027–2028, covering data-centre campuses, clean energy, water security and training.

The Reuters report says new campuses are planned in Selangor and Negeri Sembilan, alongside the existing operational Elmina campus. These are company plans reported by Reuters, not independently established future spending.
research.analysis: The plan expands regional computing capacity while increasing capital and infrastructure commitments. It does not establish new revenue, utilisation or investment returns.
research.risks: Construction, power and water availability, customer utilisation and returns on capital remain execution risks. A matching original issuer release was not retrieved.
research.next_watch: An accessible original company statement, construction milestones, commissioning dates and subsequent capital-spending disclosure.

rows.name: Meta Platforms

research.headline: Meta launches euro bond offering; SEC terms remain preliminary
facts: Reuters reports that books opened for Meta’s first euro bond sale, with maturities ranging from four to 38 years, citing a lead-manager memo. The English syndication was updated at 09:01:41 UTC.

Meta’s 424B5, accepted by the SEC at 11:01:27 UTC, describes six proposed senior-note series. Euro amounts, coupons and final maturity dates remain blank; proceeds are intended for general corporate purposes.
The filing separately confirms the previously covered US$15 billion dollar-note pricing. It does not confirm either offering has settled.
research.analysis: Euro borrowing can diversify funding sources, but the preliminary filing cannot establish final financing cost or completed funding.
research.risks: Pricing, interest expense, currency exposure and completion remain uncertain. The Reuters memo’s maturity range is distinct from the unfilled primary-document fields.
research.next_watch: Final euro pricing terms, the completed prospectus and issuer confirmation of settlement.
